inputs.text: Hey, in Cyprus the right-wing push is intensifying to weaken judicial oversight in surveillance laws, letting security forces operate with far less accountability. This comes after lawyers raised alarms on Monday, and now Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides has stepped in following a closed House session to challenge the amended bill. It's headed for a vote in the House plenum on Thursday, and blocking these changes is essential to stop further erosion of civil liberties that historically hit marginalized communities, workers, and progressive voices the hardest. Far from strengthening anything, removing these protections risks turning surveillance into a tool for reinforcing inequality and suppressing dissent from those already facing structural barriers.
